_readme: The work shown on the co-development page and on each person's profile. Every piece is credited to one person (by, their slug in team.json) and filed under one discipline. image is a file in source/work without its extension; video is an optional clip in assets/video that plays in its place when opened; set (optional) groups related pieces by one person in one discipline, such as every board for one character, into a single card whose first piece is the cover, stepped through in the viewer. The sets list names each one. Client work never goes here: only Out of Water and the team's own portfolio pieces.

disciplines.name: Concept art
disciplines.summary: Characters, creatures, props and places, drawn to explain how something plays as well as how it looks.
disciplines.body: We design for the team that has to build it. A board shows the pose, the states it moves through in game and the pieces a 3D artist needs, so the model can be started from the sheet rather than from a conversation.
includes: Character, creature, costume and prop design
Turnarounds and construction sheets ready to model from
Motion tests for anything that moves or opens

disciplines.name: Stylised 3D
disciplines.summary: Environments, props and characters with clear shapes and a lot of personality.
disciplines.body: Chunky silhouettes, hand-painted materials and budgets that survive a real frame rate. We build modular kits so a level can be dressed from a palette, and hero pieces for the places a player stops and looks.
includes: Blockout and greybox dressing through to final art
Modular environment kits and hero props
Game-ready assets for Unity or Unreal

disciplines.name: Hard surface
disciplines.summary: Vehicles, weapons and mechanical props, modelled accurately from reference.
disciplines.body: Clean topology, careful panel work and materials that hold up when the camera gets close. Garrett came to games from realistic vehicle art, so cars in particular are home ground.
includes: Vehicles from blockout to showroom render
Weapons, helmets and mechanical hero props
High to low bakes with predictable topology
PBR materials authored in the Substance tools

disciplines.name: Design and code
disciplines.summary: Level design, game and narrative design, and gameplay programming.
disciplines.body: We build levels from blockout to scripted polish in Unity and Unreal, write gameplay code in C#, and write the words characters say. A lot of what we know about feel comes from tuning two very different animals to share one screen.
includes: Level design in Unity and Unreal
Gameplay programming in Unity (C#), including enemy AI and player systems

pieces.title: The Elder Turtle
pieces.alt: Concept board for the Elder Turtle: a translucent blue spirit turtle holding a glowing trident, beside two views of the stone statue it becomes, with design notes and an invented script.
pieces.note: The guide the players meet on Chelonia, as a spirit and as the statue it lives in, with the ancient script used on its shrines.

pieces.title: Statue design process
pieces.alt: A board of pose thumbnails for the Elder Turtle statue, narrowing through iterations to a final design shown mossy, cracked and restored.
pieces.note: From rough pose thumbnails to the final statue, drawn in the three states the game moves it through.

pieces.title: Statue construction sheet
pieces.alt: A construction sheet for the statue plinth: turnaround, base and archway patterns, the spinning keyhole mechanism, and the plinth as ruined, cleaned and restored stone.
pieces.note: Everything the 3D team needed to build the plinth, including the keyhole mechanism, with a short animated test of the crystal key turning.

pieces.title: Accessories and collectables
pieces.alt: A design sheet of a glowing sargassum wreath, a crown-shaped head pattern, fluorescent shell markings and barnacle and pearl collectables, each beside its sea turtle photo reference.
pieces.note: Each piece is drawn beside the real sea turtle reference it came from.

pieces.title: Shell iconography and boss crystals
pieces.alt: The Elder Turtle's shell pattern numbered one to five, five gold crystals for the beach, forest, poison, lava and cave levels, a painted opal texture and line drawings of the shell.
pieces.note: One crystal per area, each tied to a segment of the Elder Turtle's shell.

pieces.title: The Blob King
pieces.alt: Concept board for the Blob King, a huge, grumpy pink blobfish draped in folds like a cape, shown in normal and faded skin, with his jewelled livery collar, a blue and gold conch shell and a pink and gold crown.
pieces.note: King of the Blobfish, who brings a new faction and new ways to get around. The board covers his crown, his livery collar and the ancient conch the Elder Turtle gave him to keep.

pieces.title: Blob King turnaround
pieces.alt: Front, side and back views of the Blob King in flat grey, above a blockout that picks out each layer of his folds in a different colour.
pieces.note: Each fold is designed like a piece of clothing, so the model keeps simple topology and the animators still get layers to move.

pieces.title: Blob King expressions
pieces.alt: Twelve grey sketches of the Blob King sulking, scowling, sighing and slumping, his whole body warping with each expression.
pieces.note: Gesture and expression sketches, after sarcastic and grumpy live-action characters, showing how far his body and face can bend to sell a line.

pieces.title: Mini blobfish
pieces.alt: A board of small pink blobfish used as bounce platforms: an airflip blob shown activated and at rest, a wall blob and a large, flat floor blob, each from several angles.
pieces.note: Bounce platforms in three kinds: an airflip blob that leaps up when you hit it, a wall blob that clings to walls and ceilings, and a heavy floor blob that needs both players' weight.

pieces.title: Coral Quarters
pieces.alt: A stylised wooden beach shack on stilts with a purple shingle roof and a painted dolphin sign, with palm trees and rocks behind it.
pieces.note: A beach shack built as a hero location, with hand-painted timber and shingles.

pieces.title: Coral Quarters props
pieces.alt: The Coral Quarters prop set laid out on sand: a wooden frame, solar panel, life ring, rope, noticeboards, crates, a kayak and paddles and the dolphin sign.
pieces.note: The modular set that dresses the shack, every piece reusable across the scene.

pieces.title: Witch's hut
pieces.alt: A witch's hut shaped like a cauldron under a slumping hat roof, wrapped in pale roots, on a lantern-lit jetty in blue forest mist.
pieces.note: A team environment made to a strict budget: 35,000 triangles, 2K and 1K textures, modular throughout. Martin built everything but the lighting.

pieces.title: Relic
pieces.alt: A friendly orange robot shown from three angles, with a cartoon face on a boxy screen head and thin jointed legs.
pieces.note: A personal character piece: worn materials, a deliberately lopsided build and a face that does most of the work.

pieces.title: Grunt Crab
pieces.alt: Front and back views of a round red crab with a pitted shell pulled low over wide, worried eyes, its claws raised.
pieces.note: The bulk of the spider crab's army. The cannon and shield crabs are built on the same body.

pieces.title: Cannon Crab
pieces.alt: Front and back views of the round red grunt crab with a big yellow cannon strapped to its shell by a leather belt.
pieces.note: A grunt with artillery. It fires coconuts.

pieces.title: Shield Crab
pieces.alt: A red crab crouched behind a shield of broken wooden planks daubed with a yellow and teal face, seen from the front and from behind.
pieces.note: Hides behind a face it painted itself.

pieces.title: Patrol Crab
pieces.alt: Front and back views of a flat red crab under a navy and gold pirate tricorn with a green feather, a curved white hook strapped to each claw.
pieces.note: Dressed as a pirate in whatever it could scavenge, like the rest of the army.

pieces.title: Chase Crab
pieces.alt: Two views of a long-legged red crab with a teal patterned bandana tied round its shell and one claw much bigger than the other.
pieces.note: Long in the leg, for the crab that gives chase.

pieces.title: Hootsworth
pieces.alt: Front and back views of an owl with outstretched brown wings, in a pink top hat, a pink waistcoat with gold buttons and a pink bow tie.
pieces.note: The owl who runs the hat stall and takes payment in sand dollars.

pieces.title: Mortimer
pieces.alt: Front and back views of a grey mole in a straw hat with a red band, round glasses, a red neckerchief and a cream explorer's waistcoat, with a sack slung on the back.
pieces.note: A turnaround, so the explorer's kit reads from both sides.

pieces.title: Parrot NPC, yellow
pieces.alt: Front and back views of a round yellow and white parrot in a navy pirate tricorn with gold trim and a leather bandolier, its wings spread.
pieces.note: One of three colourways.

pieces.title: Parrot NPC, blue
pieces.alt: Front and back views of the pirate parrot in blue and yellow, with purple tail feathers.
pieces.note: One of three colourways.

pieces.title: Parrot NPC, green
pieces.alt: Front and back views of the pirate parrot in green and yellow.
pieces.note: One of three colourways.

pieces.title: Wasteland hunter
pieces.alt: Front and back views of a stylised hunter in a dark waistcoat and leather straps, holding a bone claw, with a horned basilisk skull on her shoulder.
pieces.note: Concept by Yvonne Veka. Sculpted in ZBrush, hard surface in Maya, textured in Substance Painter.

pieces.title: Grimgrin the Ha-Bringer
pieces.alt: A grinning cel-shaded jester automaton in a blue and gold hat, lit by a crystal ball inside a fortune teller's booth at night.
pieces.note: A fortune teller in an inked, cel-shaded style. Modelled in Maya, textured in Substance Painter, rendered in Unreal Engine 5.

pieces.title: Tactical helmet
pieces.alt: Six views of a dark sci-fi helmet on a mannequin bust, with a tinted visor under angular plates, a ribbed respirator and a headlamp at the temple.
pieces.note: After the Cyberpunk 2077: Trauma Team comics. A turnaround, so the plating reads from every side.

pieces.title: 1973 Datsun 240Z
pieces.alt: A metallic blue 1973 Datsun 240Z parked across double yellow lines on a wooded road.
pieces.note: A final-year vehicle project, modelled from reference from blockout to render.

pieces.title: DeLorean DMC-12
pieces.alt: A brushed steel DeLorean DMC-12 on a sunlit woodland road with wildflowers in front of it.
pieces.note: Retextured from scratch, with base materials authored in Substance Designer.

pieces.title: CyberStation
pieces.alt: An isometric neon space station with trains of glowing carriages and a management interface along the top.
pieces.note: A station management game, with its simulation running end to end.

pieces.title: Gridlock
pieces.alt: A minimal strategy game on a dark grid where coloured houses send lines of units at each other.
pieces.note: A minimalist real-time strategy game: unit flow, pathfinding and an opposing AI.
